timeline.text: Patricia Young presents with profuse diarrhea with hypotension. The Chief Concern card lists profuse diarrhea with hypotension.
The nurse notes recent broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure and profuse watery diarrhea. Pain, Weight, Height, and SpO2 are documented in the vital signs card.
New results show objective deterioration and priority diagnostic support. The findings support fulminant Clostridioides difficile colitis with shock and megacolon risk.
Orders include start contact enteric precautions and administer ordered oral or rectal vancomycin plus IV metronidazole per protocol. The nurse avoids give antimotility medication routinely.
Initial treatment is underway and the client is reassessed. The priority response shows early clinical improvement.

Final evaluation shows improvement while unresolved risks remain. Ongoing follow-up is needed because fulminant c difficile requires isolation, targeted therapy, resuscitation, and surgical awareness.

end_of_case_debrief.clinical_judgment_map: Cues evolve toward postpartum preeclampsia with severe features and pulmonary edema, requiring cue recognition, analysis, prioritized hypothesis selection, targeted solutions, immediate action, and outcome evaluation.
end_of_case_debrief.missed_cues: Progression cues may look subtle until objective data confirms deterioration.
end_of_case_debrief.priority_trap: The learner may choose a familiar but less urgent explanation instead of the dangerous trend.
end_of_case_debrief.safety_lesson: Escalate early, avoid contraindicated actions, and reassess after every intervention.
end_of_case_debrief.outcome_interpretation: Improvement in one finding does not mean the high-progression case is resolved.
end_of_case_debrief.next_time_rule: Preeclampsia can worsen after delivery, especially with headache, severe BP, and pulmonary edema.
